prospect.name: Colt Campbell
prospect.occupation: Appointment setter at acquisition.com (moving to closer); also owns rental properties and hosts a music festival
prospect.family_status: Single; lives on the family farm he was raised on; supports his mother; father died 2017
prospect.training_background: Lifts at a gym ~5 days/week, ~10 hours/week including drive time; down 21 lb in 9 weeks since May 1; previously in shape at 220-225 lb with visible abs
prospect.medical: Born with asthma; says it is now largely controlled without medication, but had a severe asthma episode after 2017-18 in which he nearly died and was hospitalised for about a week, after which he was afraid to train or run

signals: Was in shape at 220-225 lb, lost it over 18-24 months after three family deaths and a near-fatal asthma attack
Explicitly describes adopting a new identity — 'this is my life now' — and then restarting
Wants the former physical self back: 'I want to get down to like somewhere between 220, 230'

goals.text: Lose a further 35-40 lb to reach roughly 220-230 lb
Longevity and functional capacity — not looking healthy but being healthy
Endurance/stamina — be able to run three miles without being wrecked
Confidence that comes from knowing he is physically capable of whatever comes up
Train far more efficiently — cut 10 hours a week in the gym down to about two
Not end up like his father, who was stiff and in pain by 50 and dead at 64

pains.text: Self-sabotage — describes deliberately holding himself back so as not to disrupt the narrative of not deserving more
Fear of the unknown stops him acting on decisions he already knows are right (moving to Texas, going all in on fitness)
Diet cycle — a month of discipline, a 'deserved' cheat day that becomes four, then two weeks of progress lost
Spends roughly ten hours a week training, which he views as time he could be earning or reading
Lost most of a decade of fitness after three family deaths in 2017-18 and a near-fatal asthma attack that left him afraid to exercise
Feels dragged down by the people around him in rural Michigan and describes himself as a loner
Feels responsible for staying in Michigan for his mother, which conflicts with what he says he wants
History of asthma including a hospitalisation, which made him afraid to train or run

objections.raw_quote: And when do you prefer an answer? Because I'm not giving you one right now.
objections.rep_response: Asked 'Why not?', then took no decision, moved to a 1-10 rating question and kept probing rather than closing

objections.raw_quote: I mean, 6,000 obviously is no small amount. mean, don't get me wrong. If I lost 6,000 right now, it'd stay like I'd be okay. It'd sting a little, but I'd be okay.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate the objection or run any financial-picture questions; asked for pros and cons instead

objections.raw_quote: Hell, for $6,000, I could hire a personal trainer that would do this with me, you know, hold me accountable, do all these other things for longer.
objections.rep_response: Teased him lightly ('Would that be from somebody from, like, me again?'), then reframed away from an hourly-rate comparison using an Alex Hormozi anecdote

objections.raw_quote: It's hard to grasp that you can get in, like, great shape in, like, an hour and a half a week of training. That's hard to grasp.
objections.rep_response: Asked a hypothetical certainty question — 'if you knew for 100% for certain... would it be like Michael here's my credit card' — but offered no proof, case studies or client evidence

objections.raw_quote: As far as why I'm not pulling the trigger on $1,200 right now, it doesn't mean it's the best process, but it's my process.
objections.rep_response: Asked whether his decision process had got him where he wanted to be and what the benefit of kicking the can down the road was; prospect conceded the logic but still did not buy

offer.payment_plan_terms: Up to three payments of $2,000 ($2K/$2K/$2K), totalling $6,000

prospect_financials.note: Self-reports over six figures a year, monthly overhead about $1,100-1,200, paid $20,000 cash for a car, owns rental properties, grosses roughly $200,000 from an annual music festival; said losing $6,000 would sting but be survivable

evidence: Prospect declined twice to decide on the call: 'I'm not saying I'm going to spend $6,000 right here on a whim.'
Declined the improvised one-month trial: 'This very second? No, I'm not doing it right now.'
Rep ended it open: 'If you decide to go for it, shoot me a text, and we'll go from there.'
Counter-evidence: prospect rated the programme 8-8.5/10 and said 'I would be inclined to agree with you' — high interest without commitment
No payment taken and no payment link mentioned
outcome.next_step: Prospect to text the rep if he decides to proceed; no follow-up call, date or link was set

notable.note: Rep improvised a $1,200 one-month trial that is not one of the two standard tiers, and made it conditional on buying immediately. He also used the prospect's own sales job against him ('the objections you give the world are the objections that you get') and framed the prospect's home town as gravitational drag. The prospect's near-fatal asthma history was volunteered and never explored for training safety.

quality.notes: Frequent mid-turn attribution swaps throughout: rep questions repeatedly appear appended to the prospect's block (e.g. 'Why is that important, though, to have that confidence' at 00:19:08 is inside a Colt block, and 'Can I make you a deal, dude?' at 01:07 sits at the end of a Colt block). Role was read from content throughout.
